About Us

Vertex Service Partners is a home improvement services company focused on residential roofing and other exterior services across the United States. Backed by Alpine Investors, a top-decile private equity fund with $4.0 billion of committed capital, Vertex is building a best-in-class national platform. Our company is built on our core values—servant leadership, unwavering character, a growth mindset, persistence, empowerment, pace, and fun—and guided by three pillars: being the Employer of Choice, Partner of Choice, and Contractor of Choice. We offer transformative support in operations, marketing, training, talent, finance, and technology, all while preserving the autonomy of local brands.

Mission of the role 

As a Junior AI Engineer on the AI Engineering team, you help build the AI-powered applications, automations, and models our brands use every day: tools that route leads to sales reps, calculate commissions, staff call centers, onboard and offboard field employees, and deliver the morning reports leadership relies on. Working alongside the Senior Manager of AI Engineering, you take features from request to production. You gather context from the business, build with AI-assisted development (e.g., Claude Code), connect to our business systems and data warehouse, and prove your work with tests before it ships. You start on well-scoped pieces of live applications and grow into owning features, LLM capabilities, and machine learning models end-to-end. 

Where you'll make an impact 

Internal applications — Build and improve full-stack web applications in TypeScript, React, and Node on Postgres using AI coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code), working in GitHub with pull requests, code review, and CI/CD. 
LLM-powered features — Ship features built on large language models (e.g., the Claude API and Snowflake Cortex), such as plain-English summaries in automated reports, in-app assistants that answer “how do I…” questions, and routing requests to the right team. Evaluate the output so quality is measured, not assumed. 
Machine learning — Help train, deploy, and monitor predictive models in our data warehouse, such as lead-to-rep matching scores and revenue predictions, including scheduled scoring and retraining. 
System integrations — Connect our applications to the platforms the business runs on, including field-service management, HR and payroll, recruiting, sales/CRM, SMS, and email. Make those integrations safe to re-run, resilient to failure, and easy to audit. 
Data modeling in dbt — Write dbt models in SQL with the help of AI coding assistants while understanding the dbt methodology yourself: declaring sources, layering staging, intermediate, and mart models, building the DAG with ref(), choosing materializations (view, table, incremental), and adding tests and documentation in YAML. Know how data flows from raw source to the mart an app or report reads, and what breaks downstream when a model changes. 
Reporting & alerting automation — Build scheduled reports, data-quality checks, and watchdogs (Python, serverless functions) that tell the right people when something has gone wrong in the business or in one of our own services. 
Cloud deployment & operations — Deploy and run services on Azure (App Service, Functions, Key Vault, Entra ID sign-in, Application Insights) and help keep them healthy once they are live. 
Business partnership — Work directly with sales, operations, recruiting, and finance users to understand what they need, demo what you built, and document it so others can support it. 

Key outcomes 

Ships to production early — Delivers small, reviewed changes to live applications in the first month and owns a feature end-to-end by the end of the first quarter. 
Capacity multiplier — Takes well-defined features, fixes, and enhancements off senior engineering's plate so senior time goes to architecture and the hardest problems. 
Reliable, tested work — Changes ship with tests and documentation; integrations don't double-send, double-pay, or fail silently. 
Measured AI — LLM and ML features have an evaluation set or a before/after measurement, so we know they work. 
Trusted by users — The business teams who use our tools see their requests understood, delivered, and followed up on. 

This role allows you to 

Put AI into production. Sales reps, managers, and executives use your work every day; it doesn't sit in a demo. 
Learn full-stack, data, and applied-AI engineering at the same time, with direct mentorship from a senior AI engineering leader. 
Build with modern AI-assisted tooling and learn how to direct it, review it, and ship it responsibly. 
Grow quickly in a collaborative, entrepreneurial, fast-growing company. 

Who you are 

You have 0–2 years of professional software, data, or AI engineering experience, or a CS/engineering degree, bootcamp, or equivalent portfolio. 
You write working Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, and solid SQL (joins, CTEs, window functions, CASE statements). 
You have built and deployed at least one project that someone other than you has used. 
You have called an LLM API from code (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar) and understand prompts, tool use, and the limits of model output. 
You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) daily, and you review, test, and question what they produce rather than accepting it as-is. 
You're comfortable with Git/GitHub: small commits, clear pull requests, and having your code reviewed and iterating on feedback. 
You understand, or can quickly learn, how data moves from source systems through modeled layers in a data warehouse. 
You're a clear communicator who can explain a technical fix to a non-technical manager in a couple of sentences. 
You're curious about how the business runs and enjoy turning a vague request into something that works. 

Nice to have 

dbt, Snowflake, or a modern data stack. 
React (Tailwind, TanStack Query) and Postgres with an ORM. 
Azure or another major cloud (serverless functions, app hosting, identity). 
ML fundamentals: training, evaluating, and serving a classification or regression model. 
RAG, agent, or tool-use patterns with LLMs, and evaluating LLM output. 
Automated testing (Vitest/Jest, pytest, Playwright). 
Field-service, home services, or multi-site experience. 

Personal characteristics 

Data-driven decision-maker — Skilled at working with data and finding meaning and action in numbers. 
Flexible & adaptable — Willing to take on new projects and challenges to support the evolving needs of a high-growth company. 
Get-it-done attitude — Problem-solves on the fly and completes time-sensitive work to drive the business forward. 
Service-oriented — Builds strong relationships with peers across the corporate team and operating companies. 
Resourceful — Drives action and achieves results creatively with finite resources. 
Critical thinker and learner — Picks things up quickly and asks “why” rather than taking “yes” for an answer. 
Culture carrier — A humble servant leader with unyielding integrity who is self-aware, open to feedback, and respectful of others. 

Benefits:

Full-time employees are eligible to participate in the following benefits:

Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance
401(k) with company match
Company sponsored Life and AD&D coverage
Paid Time Off
Opportunities for growth and on-the-job training

Why Join Us?

Build Something Big – Shape processes for a rapidly growing organization.
Growth-Oriented Culture – Work in a dynamic, people-first environment.
Make an Impact Across Regions – Partner with business leaders to drive meaningful change.

Apply Today!

As a government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA), we request this information in order to measure the effectiveness of the outreach and positive recruitment efforts we undertake pursuant to VEVRAA. Classification of protected categories is as follows:

A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: a veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs; or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.

A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.

An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.

An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

Why are you being asked to complete this form?

We are a federal contractor or subcontractor. The law requires us to provide equal employment opportunity to qualified people with disabilities. We have a goal of having at least 7% of our workers as people with disabilities. The law says we must measure our progress towards this goal. To do this, we must ask applicants and employees if they have a disability or have ever had one. People can become disabled, so we need to ask this question at least every five years.

Completing this form is voluntary, and we hope that you will choose to do so. Your answer is confidential. No one who makes hiring decisions will see it. Your decision to complete the form and your answer will not harm you in any way. If you want to learn more about the law or this form, visit the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) website at www.dol.gov/ofccp.

How do you know if you have a disability?

A disability is a condition that substantially limits one or more of your “major life activities.” If you have or have ever had such a condition, you are a person with a disability. Disabilities include, but are not limited to:

Alcohol or other substance use disorder (not currently using drugs illegally)
Autoimmune disorder, for example, lupus, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, HIV/AIDS
Blind or low vision
Cancer (past or present)
Cardiovascular or heart disease
Celiac disease
Cerebral palsy
Deaf or serious difficulty hearing
Diabetes
Disfigurement, for example, disfigurement caused by burns, wounds, accidents, or congenital disorders
Epilepsy or other seizure disorder
Gastrointestinal disorders, for example, Crohn's Disease, irritable bowel syndrome
Intellectual or developmental disability
Mental health conditions, for example, depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, PTSD
Missing limbs or partially missing limbs
Mobility impairment, benefiting from the use of a wheelchair, scooter, walker, leg brace(s) and/or other supports
Nervous system condition, for example, migraine headaches, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis (MS)
Neurodivergence, for example, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, dyspraxia, other learning disabilities
Partial or complete paralysis (any cause)
Pulmonary or respiratory conditions, for example, tuberculosis, asthma, emphysema
Short stature (dwarfism)
Traumatic brain injury
